sections.title: 1. Genesis of the Act: The Executive-Judicial Conflict (1773-1781)

masteryZone.q: The severe conflict between the Supreme Court and the Governor-General-in-Council in Bengal during 1774-1781 was primarily due to:
opts: Vague and overlapping jurisdictions in the Regulating Act of 1773
A dispute over the selection of the Chief Justice
The refusal of the Governor-General to pay judicial salaries
The Supreme Court's alliance with French authorities in Chandernagore
masteryZone.sol: The Regulating Act of 1773 did not clearly define the boundary of jurisdiction between the newly established Supreme Court and the Governor-General-in-Council, leading to massive clashes.

masteryZone.q: In which specific dispute did the Supreme Court issue a writ of arrest against a Zamindar, prompting Warren Hastings to deploy EIC military troops to arrest the court's bailiffs?
opts: The Patna Case
The Cossijurah Case
The trial of Raja Nandakumar
The Kamaluddin Case
masteryZone.sol: In the Cossijurah Case, EIC military forces blocked the execution of a Supreme Court warrant against the Zamindar, highlighting the severe executive-judicial crisis.

masteryZone.q: The Supreme Court of Calcutta's early practice of applying English common law to native populations led to which highly criticized trial, widely described as 'judicial murder'?
opts: The Patna Case
The Trial of Raja Nandakumar
The Cossijurah Case
The Benares Insurrection Trial
masteryZone.sol: In 1775, Raja Nandakumar was executed under English forgery law, which was not applicable to native Indians, triggering severe criticism and accusations of 'judicial murder'.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following EIC offices/bodies was Warren Hastings heading when the clashes with the Supreme Court reached their peak?
opts: Governor-General-in-Council of Bengal
Board of Control
Court of Directors
Sadar Diwani Adalat exclusively
masteryZone.sol: Warren Hastings was the head of the Governor-General-in-Council of Bengal, which functioned as the executive administration.

masteryZone.q: The Patna Case (1777-1779) primarily exposed the conflict between the Supreme Court and which provincial bodies?
opts: Provincial revenue councils acting as local courts
The local Zamindars' private councils
The French trade administrators
The Mughal imperial courts
masteryZone.sol: The Patna Case arose from the Supreme Court penalizing local officers acting under the authority of the EIC Provincial Revenue Council of Patna, exposing local-judicial conflicts.

masteryZone.q: Identify the primary reasons for the conflicts between the Governor-General-in-Council and the Supreme Court between 1774 and 1781: (Select all that apply)
opts: Vague definition of 'British subjects' under the Regulating Act of 1773
Overlap of jurisdiction over revenue collectors and local Zamindars
The Supreme Court's attempt to apply English common law to native Indians
The Governor-General's attempts to dissolve the Supreme Court
masteryZone.sol: The conflicts were driven by vague definitions of British subjects, jurisdiction over revenue systems/Zamindars, and the direct application of English common law to native custom. The GG had no power to dissolve the Supreme Court.

masteryZone.q: Select the historical cases that directly influenced the British Parliament to pass the Act of Settlement 1781: (Select all that apply)
opts: Trial of Raja Nandakumar
The Patna Case
The Cossijurah Case
The impeachment of Warren Hastings
masteryZone.sol: The Trial of Nandakumar, Patna Case, and Cossijurah Case were the three main conflict cases that prompted the passage of the 1781 Act. Impeachment occurred much later in London.

masteryZone.q: Which bodies or classes of people in Bengal complained about the Supreme Court's jurisdiction before 1781? (Select all that apply)
opts: East India Company officials and revenue collectors
British merchants and residents in Calcutta
Local land-owning Zamindars
The French East India Company
masteryZone.sol: EIC officials, British merchants in Calcutta, and local Zamindars all sent petitions to the British Parliament complaining about the Court's high-handedness.

masteryZone.q: What were the major legal issues in the Patna Case? (Select all that apply)
opts: The Supreme Court claimed jurisdiction over native officers working for EIC councils
The Court applied English common law procedures to a native inheritance dispute
The EIC officers were held personally liable for damages for executing an EIC warrant
The dispute involved the inheritance of the Nawab of Bengal
masteryZone.sol: The case involved inheritance but for a wealthy native merchant, not the Nawab. The court asserted jurisdiction over EIC native officers and held them personally liable under English law.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following describe Sir Elijah Impey's role in the executive-judicial standoff? (Select all that apply)
opts: He served as the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Calcutta
He was a close school friend of Warren Hastings, which complicated the conflict
He was later appointed by Hastings to head the Sadar Diwani Adalat in a compromise
He served as the commander of EIC military forces
masteryZone.sol: Impey was Chief Justice, a friend of Hastings, and was later appointed to head the Sadar Diwani Adalat in an attempt to buy peace, which led to Impey's recall to England. He had no military command.

masteryZone.q: The Regulating Act of 1773 explicitly stated that native Zamindars were subject to the Supreme Court's jurisdiction.
masteryZone.sol: The Regulating Act of 1773 was completely silent on whether local native Zamindars were subject to the Court, leading to the conflict.

masteryZone.q: The Patna Case involved a dispute over inheritance between a widow and her deceased husband's nephew.
masteryZone.sol: True. The Patna Case began as a domestic inheritance dispute under Muslim personal law, which EIC revenue officers arbitrated, leading to the Supreme Court's intervention.

masteryZone.q: The Cossijurah Case resulted in an armed standoff between the Governor-General's troops and the Supreme Court sheriff's men.
masteryZone.sol: True. EIC troops intercepted and arrested the Sheriff's bailiffs, marking the peak of physical confrontation between the executive and judiciary.

masteryZone.q: The Touchet Committee was appointed by the King of England without parliamentary oversight.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Touchet Committee was a select committee appointed by the British House of Commons (Parliament).

masteryZone.q: Raja Nandakumar was executed for a crime committed before the Supreme Court was established.
masteryZone.sol: True. He was executed under a British act for forgery committed in 1769, long before the Supreme Court was set up in 1774, which made it highly controversial.

masteryZone.q: Warren Hastings and Chief Justice Sir Elijah Impey maintained a smooth cooperative relationship throughout 1774-1781.
masteryZone.sol: False. They had extremely tense relations and clashed repeatedly until Hastings compromised by offering Impey the presidency of the Sadar Diwani Adalat.

masteryZone.q: The British Parliament did not receive any petitions from Calcutta concerning the Supreme Court's jurisdiction.
masteryZone.sol: False. Parliament received major petitions from EIC servants and British merchants in Calcutta, complaining about the Supreme Court.

masteryZone.q: The Patna Revenue Council consisted of native officers who were assisted by Muslim law officers (Muftis and Qazis).
masteryZone.sol: True. The council relied on native law officers to determine Islamic inheritance rules.

masteryZone.q: The Supreme Court of Calcutta was established in the year ___________.
masteryZone.sol: The Regulating Act was passed in 1773, and the Supreme Court was set up in Calcutta in 1774.

masteryZone.q: The armed confrontation between EIC military forces and Supreme Court bailiffs occurred during the ___________ Case.
masteryZone.sol: The Cossijurah Case saw Hastings order Company troops to arrest Supreme Court officers.

masteryZone.q: Raja Nandakumar was sentenced to death for the crime of ___________.
masteryZone.sol: He was executed for forgery, a capital offense under English law but not under native laws.

masteryZone.q: The select committee of the House of Commons that investigated the Bengal judicial crisis was the ___________ Committee.
masteryZone.sol: The Touchet Committee investigated the petitions and drafted the report leading to the Amending Act.

masteryZone.q: Sir Elijah Impey was appointed to head the EIC's supreme civil court, the Sadar ___________ Adalat.
masteryZone.sol: Hastings appointed Impey as the judge of the Sadar Diwani Adalat in 1780 to defuse the conflict.

masteryZone.q: The Governor-General of Bengal whose executive actions were challenged by the Supreme Court was ___________.
masteryZone.sol: Warren Hastings led the executive during this entire conflict phase.

masteryZone.q: The Cossijurah Case involved a wealthy local ___________ whose revenue collections were critical for the EIC.
masteryZone.sol: The Raja of Cossijurah was a local Zamindar whose revenue EIC wanted to protect from Court attachments.

masteryZone.q: The Patna Case involved local native law officers who were arrested by order of the ___________ Court.
masteryZone.sol: The Supreme Court ordered the arrest of the Qazis and Muftis of the Patna council.

masteryZone.q: Match the cases with their corresponding legal significance:

options.text: A. Application of English forgery law on native Indians
B. Stave-off between Supreme Court and EIC provincial revenue officers
C. Armed conflict between EIC military and Supreme Court bailiffs

masteryZone.sol: Nandakumar involved English forgery law; Patna Case involved EIC revenue officers; Cossijurah Case involved EIC military vs Court bailiffs.

masteryZone.q: Match the historical figures with their roles during the constitutional crisis (1773-1781):

options.text: A. Governor-General of Bengal defending executive supremacy
B. Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Calcutta
C. Head of the Parliamentary Select Committee investigating EIC petitions

masteryZone.sol: Hastings was Governor-General; Impey was Chief Justice; Touchet headed the select committee.

masteryZone.q: Match the institutions with their legal jurisdictions under the 1773 setup:

options.text: A. Crown-established court administering English Common Law
B. EIC-established appellate civil court headed by the GG-in-Council
C. Local EIC bodies collecting revenue and arbitrating native disputes

masteryZone.sol: Supreme Court was Crown-established; Sadar Diwani Adalat was EIC appellate court under GG; Provincial Councils handled revenue/local disputes.

masteryZone.q: What did the Supreme Court of Calcutta claim in order to summon native Zamindars?
masteryZone.sol: It claimed they were 'servants of the Company' directly or indirectly due to their revenue duties.

masteryZone.q: Why did EIC revenue collectors fear the Supreme Court during 1774-1781?
masteryZone.sol: Because they were sued personally in the Court for damages for performing their EIC revenue duties.

masteryZone.q: How did Warren Hastings respond to the Supreme Court's writ in the Cossijurah Case?
masteryZone.sol: He ordered EIC military forces to block the Court bailiffs and arrest them.

masteryZone.q: Name the petition that triggered the parliament to form the Touchet Committee.
masteryZone.sol: The petition of EIC servants and British inhabitants of Calcutta in 1780.

masteryZone.q: Who was the native noble whose trial for forgery became the symbol of judicial overreach?
masteryZone.sol: Raja Nandakumar.

masteryZone.q: What was the legal system applied by the Supreme Court of Calcutta initially?
masteryZone.sol: English Common Law and equity rules.

masteryZone.q: What EIC provincial council was sued in the Patna Case?
masteryZone.sol: The Patna Provincial Council.

masteryZone.q: What parliamentary act established the Calcutta Supreme Court?
masteryZone.sol: The Regulating Act of 1773.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Regulating Act of 1773 created a system of checks and balances in Bengal.
Reason (R): It failed to define the boundaries of jurisdiction, causing a total breakdown of administration.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true. The Act intended checks and balances, but its failure to define jurisdictions led to administrative breakdown. R is not the correct explanation of why it was created.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Warren Hastings appointed Sir Elijah Impey as judge of the Sadar Diwani Adalat in 1780.
Reason (R): Hastings wanted to bribe the Chief Justice to prevent further interference in executive affairs.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R is the correct explanation. Hastings offered the salaried post of Sadar Diwani Adalat head to Impey as a political compromise to stop Supreme Court challenges.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): EIC forces arrested the Supreme Court's officers in the Cossijurah Case.
Reason (R): The Governor-General wanted to assert that EIC military power was legally superior to Crown court writs.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: A is true. R is false because Hastings' action was driven by the practical need to protect revenue collection, not to declare EIC military superior to the Crown's court.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The trial of Raja Nandakumar was conducted under English law.
Reason (R): Forgery was a capital offense in traditional Hindu and Muslim jurisprudence.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: A is true. R is false because forgery was only a minor civil wrong in traditional Indian laws, not a capital crime.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Patna Case damaged the EIC's local judicial machinery in Bengal.
Reason (R): The Supreme Court arrested local Muslim law officers (Qazis and Muftis) for performing their EIC court duties.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R is the correct explanation of A. Arresting the law officers paralyzed the provincial civil courts.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Touchet Committee supported the Supreme Court's claim of absolute jurisdiction over native Zamindars.
Reason (R): The committee recommended that the EIC administration should be kept subordinate to English Common Law.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are false. The Touchet Committee opposed the Supreme Court's absolute claims and recommended restricting its jurisdiction to protect revenue administration.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Regulating Act of 1773 failed to define what constituted 'British subjects'.
Reason (R): The Supreme Court used this vagueness to expand its jurisdiction over all native inhabitants of Bengal.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R is the correct explanation. The vague definition allowed the court to claim jurisdiction over anyone associated with EIC.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): English common law was popular among native inhabitants of Bengal in 1775.
Reason (R): English procedures were fast, cheap, and easily understood by the local population.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are false. English law was highly unpopular because it was unfamiliar, slow, expensive, and ignored local customs.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the early Supreme Court of Calcutta:
1. It was established at Fort William in Calcutta.
2. It consisted of a Chief Justice and three puisne judges.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct. The Court consisted of Chief Justice Sir Elijah Impey and three puisne judges (Chambers, Lemaistre, and Hyde) at Fort William.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Patna Case:
1. The Supreme Court awarded massive damages against EIC officers for actions taken under EIC authority.
2. It proved that the EIC's provincial administration was legally independent of the Crown's courts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Patna Case proved the opposite: EIC provincial administration was vulnerable to the Crown court.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the trial of Raja Nandakumar:
1. He was accused of forgery by a native merchant.
2. Warren Hastings was accused by Nandakumar of accepting bribes before the trial.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct. Nandakumar had accused Hastings of corruption, and shortly after, Hastings' allies brought forgery charges against Nandakumar, leading to his execution.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Cossijurah Case:
1. The Sheriff of Calcutta was supported by a large force of EIC military sepoy troops.
2. EIC forces arrested the court's bailiffs to prevent them from seizing the Zamindar's property.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect because the Sheriff was supported by private armed guards, while EIC sepoy troops arrested them under Hastings' orders.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Touchet Committee:
1. It recommended expanding the powers of the Supreme Court to check corruption.
2. It was appointed in 1781 following the petitions of the inhabitants of Bengal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect because the committee recommended restricting the Supreme Court's jurisdiction.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Regulating Act of 1773 lead to executive-judicial conflicts?
masteryZone.sol: Because it established the Supreme Court and the Governor-General-in-Council simultaneously without defining their respective jurisdictions, applicable laws, or boundary of authority.

masteryZone.q: Why did Warren Hastings order the arrest of the Supreme Court's bailiffs in the Cossijurah Case?
masteryZone.sol: Because the Supreme Court's attempt to attach the Zamindar's estate threatened EIC land revenue collection, forcing Hastings to physically protect the revenue machinery.

masteryZone.q: Why was the trial of Raja Nandakumar termed a 'judicial murder'?
masteryZone.sol: Because he was sentenced to death under an English statute against forgery that was not legally in force in India, and the trial was conducted by Hastings' close friend Chief Justice Impey shortly after Nandakumar accused Hastings of corruption.

masteryZone.q: How did the Supreme Court assert jurisdiction over native inhabitants outside Calcutta?
masteryZone.sol: By interpreting 'servants of the Company' broadly to include local Zamindars, revenue farmers, and native contractors who had transactions with EIC.

masteryZone.q: How did the EIC administration defuse the conflict in 1780 before the Amending Act was passed?
masteryZone.sol: By Warren Hastings appointing Chief Justice Sir Elijah Impey as the sole judge of the Sadar Diwani Adalat, giving him an additional salary to bring him into alignment with EIC interests.

masteryZone.q: How did the Patna Case impact the provincial judicial system of the EIC?
masteryZone.sol: The Supreme Court arrested the native law officers (Qazis and Muftis) of the Patna Council, which frightened other judicial officers and paralyzed EIC civil administration in the districts.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: In the Patna Case, the Supreme Court held that native officers were personally liable for damages because EIC charter did not authorize delegation of judicial duties to them. What does this case study show about the EIC's early legal status?
masteryZone.sol: It shows that the early EIC administration was legally weak, and its local delegation of judicial powers was not recognized by Crown courts administering English Common Law.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: During the Cossijurah standoff, the Governor-General Warren Hastings declared that the state's revenue flow could not be risked for judicial writs. What constitutional dilemma does this highlight?
masteryZone.sol: It highlights the classic constitutional dilemma between executive necessity (revenue/defense) and the rule of law (enforcing judicial writs against EIC subjects).

masteryZone.q: Case Study: In 1781, the British Parliament enacted the Amending Act, largely based on EIC revenue losses during the disputes. What does this indicate about British priorities?
masteryZone.sol: It indicates that the British Parliament prioritized protecting EIC revenues and colonial administrative stability over establishing an independent judiciary in India.

masteryZone.q: Explain the concept of 'Conflict of Jurisdictions' in early British India to a beginner.
masteryZone.sol: It is a situation where two bodies—the Governor-General's Council (EIC) and the Supreme Court (Crown)—both claim absolute authority over the same people and territory, with no clear law to decide who is superior, leading to deadlock and military standoffs.

masteryZone.q: Explain why the Patna Case is considered a landmark in Anglo-Indian legal history.
masteryZone.sol: It exposed the breakdown of the EIC's provincial court system and proved that local native officers could be personally prosecuted under English law for executing EIC administrative tasks, forcing Parliament to intervene.

masteryZone.q: Explain the role of the 'Touchet Committee' in resolving the 1773 Regulating Act defects.
masteryZone.sol: The Touchet Committee investigated the petitions of EIC officials and Calcutta citizens. It documented the paralysis of the administration and recommended that the Supreme Court's powers be restricted, leading directly to the Act of Settlement.

masteryZone.q: The separation of revenue collection from the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in 1781 primarily aimed to protect which of the following?
opts: The financial stability and revenue flow of the East India Company
The land rights of the poor tenant farmers
The independence of the judiciary
The trade monopoly of the French merchants
masteryZone.sol: By excluding revenue collection from the Supreme Court, Parliament protected EIC's financial interests, ensuring steady revenue collection without judicial interference.

masteryZone.q: Which body served as the court of final appeal in Bengal for civil disputes valued below £5,000 under the Amending Act of 1781?
opts: The Governor-General-in-Council
The Supreme Court of Judicature at Calcutta
The King-in-Council in London
The Sadar Nizamat Adalat
masteryZone.sol: The Governor-General-in-Council was designated as the appellate authority for Provincial Courts, with further appeals to the King-in-Council only allowed for disputes of £5,000 or more.

masteryZone.q: What did the Act of Settlement 1781 declare regarding EIC servants acting under the warrants of provincial courts?
opts: They were immune from prosecution in the Supreme Court for executing such warrants.
They had to obtain a license from the Supreme Court before execution.
They were subject to English common law prosecution if a native complained.
They were abolished and replaced by Crown sheriffs.
masteryZone.sol: The Act protected Company servants from being sued or prosecuted in the Supreme Court for actions taken to execute provincial court warrants.

masteryZone.q: How did the 1781 Act alter the legislative rule-making authority of the Governor-General-in-Council?
opts: It allowed them to frame regulations for provincial areas without registering them in the Supreme Court.
It took away their power to frame regulations.
It made their regulations subject to a veto by the Chief Justice.
It required all regulations to be drafted by the Supreme Court.
masteryZone.sol: The Act empowered the Governor-General-in-Council to frame regulations for provincial courts and councils without the need for registration or approval by the Supreme Court.

masteryZone.q: What was the long-term impact of the statutory recognition of personal laws in the Amending Act of 1781?
opts: It led to the codification and translation of classical Sanskrit and Arabic legal texts by British scholars.
It led to the immediate establishment of a Uniform Civil Code in India.
It restricted Indians from practicing their religions.
It caused the dissolution of native religious customs.
masteryZone.sol: To apply Hindu and Muslim personal laws, British judges commissioned translations and compilations of traditional law texts, laying the foundations of Anglo-Indian jurisprudence.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following classes of actions were exempted from Supreme Court jurisdiction by the Act of Settlement 1781? (Select all that apply)
opts: Official acts of the Governor-General and Council
Revenue collection matters and officers' actions therein
Judicial actions of provincial magistrates
Private contract disputes of EIC servants in Calcutta
masteryZone.sol: Official executive acts, revenue collections, and provincial judicial acts were exempted. Private civil disputes of EIC servants inside Calcutta remained subject to the Court.

masteryZone.q: Under the Act of 1781, how were native personal laws to be applied? (Select all that apply)
opts: Hindu personal law had to be applied to Hindu defendants
Mohammedan law had to be applied to Muslim defendants
Inheritance and contract disputes were governed by these laws
All criminal offenses were judged under Hindu and Islamic law instead of English law
masteryZone.sol: Personal laws were applied based on the defendant's religion, particularly in civil matters like inheritance and contracts. Criminal law was eventually modified, but was not completely replaced by native criminal codes in the Supreme Court.

masteryZone.q: What constitutional concepts are associated with the Amending Act of 1781? (Select all that apply)
opts: Separation of powers between executive and judiciary
Protection of revenue administration from judicial review
Statutory recognition of indigenous customs
Establishment of a federal division of powers between provinces
masteryZone.sol: The Act represents an early form of separation of powers, protection of administrative revenue, and statutory recognition of personal laws. Federal division of powers was introduced much later (1935).

masteryZone.q: Select the correct channels of appeal after the 1781 Act: (Select all that apply)
opts: Provincial Court -> Governor-General-in-Council (for cases under £5,000)
Governor-General-in-Council -> King-in-Council (for civil cases £5,000 and above)
Provincial Court -> Supreme Court of Calcutta (for all cases)
Supreme Court of Calcutta -> Governor-General-in-Council
masteryZone.sol: Appeals from provincial courts lay to the GG-in-Council, and further to the King-in-Council in England if the dispute value was £5,000 or more. The Supreme Court was bypassed.

masteryZone.q: Which EIC organs were strengthened by the Amending Act of 1781? (Select all that apply)
opts: The Governor-General-in-Council
The Provincial Courts (Mofussil Courts)
The Supreme Court of Calcutta
The Board of Control
masteryZone.sol: The GG-in-Council and the Provincial Courts were strengthened (immunized from Supreme Court writs). The Supreme Court's jurisdiction was restricted. The Board of Control was not created until 1784.

masteryZone.q: The Amending Act of 1781 declared that the Supreme Court's jurisdiction applied to the entire territory of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Act restricted the Supreme Court's direct territorial jurisdiction over native residents to the town of Calcutta.

masteryZone.q: Appeals from the Governor-General-in-Council's appellate decisions could be taken to the King-in-Council for any value.
masteryZone.sol: False. Appeals to the King-in-Council were limited to civil suits of £5,000 or more.

masteryZone.q: The Amending Act of 1781 exempted the Governor-General and Council from prosecution in England.
masteryZone.sol: False. They were only exempted from the Supreme Court in India, but could still be sued or prosecuted in the Court of King's Bench in England.

masteryZone.q: The Act of 1781 was the first British law in India to officially recognize personal laws based on religious identity.
masteryZone.sol: True. It was the first statutory parliamentary recognition of Hindu and Muslim personal laws in India.

masteryZone.q: The Supreme Court retained the power to hear cases involving revenue collection after 1781.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Act explicitly excluded revenue matters and actions in revenue collection from the Court's jurisdiction.

masteryZone.q: The Governor-General-in-Council's rules for provincial areas had to be approved by the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Act removed the requirement of registration/approval from the Supreme Court for provincial regulations.

masteryZone.q: The Act of Settlement of 1781 served to resolve administrative paralysis caused by the Regulating Act of 1773.
masteryZone.sol: True. Resolving administrative gridlocks was the primary purpose of the Act.

masteryZone.q: Under the 1781 Act, native inhabitants of Calcutta were subject to English criminal law but native civil law in inheritance.
masteryZone.sol: True. In Calcutta, criminal cases were tried under English-style rules, but personal civil matters used native personal laws.

masteryZone.q: The Amending Act of 1781 exempted the ___________ from the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court for official acts.
masteryZone.sol: The GG and his Council members received immunity for acts done in their public capacity.

masteryZone.q: Under the 1781 Act, appeals from provincial courts lay to the Governor-General-in-Council, who functioned as the Sadar ___________ Adalat.
masteryZone.sol: The Sadar Diwani Adalat heard civil appeals, while Sadar Nizamat Adalat handled criminal matters.

masteryZone.q: The minimum valuation of a civil suit required to appeal from the GG-in-Council to the King-in-Council was ___________ pounds.
masteryZone.sol: Appeals to the King-in-Council required a value of £5,000 or more.

masteryZone.q: The 1781 Act excluded ___________ matters from the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
masteryZone.sol: All revenue matters and collection activities were excluded.

masteryZone.q: For Muslim defendants, the Supreme Court was required to apply ___________ law.
masteryZone.sol: The Act mandated the application of Mohammedan (Islamic) law for Muslims.

masteryZone.q: Regulations framed by the Governor-General-in-Council for Provincial Courts did not require registration in the ___________ Court.
masteryZone.sol: The registration requirement with the Supreme Court was abolished for provincial regulations.

masteryZone.q: EIC servants were exempted from Supreme Court suits only for acts done in their ___________ capacity.
masteryZone.sol: Exemption only applied to their official capacity actions.

masteryZone.q: The Amending Act of 1781 is also known as the Act of ___________.
masteryZone.sol: It is widely known as the Act of Settlement 1781.

masteryZone.q: Match the provisions of the Amending Act of 1781 with their corresponding targets:

options.text: A. Official actions of the executive administration
B. Financial operations of EIC and collectors
C. Native Indian inhabitants of Calcutta

masteryZone.sol: GG & Council were exempted for official executive actions; revenue was excluded to protect EIC finances; personal laws applied to native inhabitants.

masteryZone.q: Match the appellate steps under the Act of 1781 hierarchy:

options.text: A. Tried initially in EIC Mofussil (Provincial) Courts
B. Decided finally by the Governor-General-in-Council
C. Can be appealed to the King-in-Council in London

masteryZone.sol: Provincial disputes began in Mofussil courts; appeals below £5,000 ended with the GG-in-Council; appeals £5,000+ went to King-in-Council.

masteryZone.q: Match the statutory changes with their constitutional impacts:

items.left: I. Removal of Supreme Court registration
III. Court restricted to Calcutta inhabitants

options.text: A. Consolidated the regulation-making authority of the executive
B. Protected EIC district courts from Supreme Court writs
C. Limited the geographical reach of English Common Law

masteryZone.sol: Removal of registration strengthened executive regulation-making; exemption of provincial judges protected district courts; restricting the court to Calcutta limited the reach of English law.

masteryZone.q: Who could sue the Governor-General for official oppression after 1781?
masteryZone.sol: A plaintiff could file a lawsuit in the Court of King's Bench in London.

masteryZone.q: What happened to the EIC's revenue collection under this Act?
masteryZone.sol: It was completely exempted from judicial review by the Supreme Court.

masteryZone.q: Why were personal laws applied in Calcutta civil trials?
masteryZone.sol: To respect native religious custom and prevent local rebellions.

masteryZone.q: Where did appeals from the Sadar Diwani Adalat go for high-value cases?
masteryZone.sol: To the King-in-Council in London.

masteryZone.q: Did EIC servants retain immunity for private crimes inside Calcutta?
masteryZone.sol: No, they remained subject to the Supreme Court's criminal jurisdiction.

masteryZone.q: Who headed the Sadar Diwani Adalat after the 1781 reforms?
masteryZone.sol: The Governor-General and members of his Council.

masteryZone.q: What legal codes were translated to assist Supreme Court judges?
masteryZone.sol: Classical Hindu and Islamic legal texts.

masteryZone.q: Did the 1781 Act introduce double government?
masteryZone.sol: No, double government was introduced by Pitt's India Act of 1784.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Amending Act of 1781 protected EIC revenue officers from judicial arrest.
Reason (R): The British government prioritized EIC's financial stability over the Supreme Court's judicial supremacy.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R explains A. EIC's revenue was vital for the British state, so they immunized revenue officers to protect collections.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Appeals from provincial civil courts lay to the Governor-General-in-Council.
Reason (R): The Supreme Court of Calcutta lacked the capability to handle native civil cases.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: A is true. R is false because the Supreme Court had the capability, but was bypassed politically to keep provincial judicial networks under EIC executive control.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Act of Settlement 1781 exempted EIC servants from the Supreme Court for their private acts.
Reason (R): Company servants were regarded as ruling elites who could not be tried under common law in India.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are false. The exemption only applied to EIC servants for their official capacities; they remained liable for private civil and criminal acts.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The 1781 Act allowed the Governor-General-in-Council to override local Hindu and Muslim customs.
Reason (R): Parliament wanted to establish English common law as the uniform civil code for all of India.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are false. The Act explicitly ordered the executive and the judiciary to respect and preserve native customs and personal laws.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Regulations made by the GG-in-Council for Provincial Courts did not require registration in the Supreme Court.
Reason (R): The registration system had led to a judicial veto and executive deadlock under the 1773 Act.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R explains A. Removing the registration requirement ended the Supreme Court's veto over provincial laws.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Supreme Court of Calcutta became a subordinate department of the EIC after 1781.
Reason (R): The Chief Justice was appointed directly by the Governor-General under the provisions of the Act.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are false. The Supreme Court remained an independent Crown court, and its judges were appointed by the King, not the Governor-General.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Amending Act of 1781 is regarded as the first statutory limit on judicial review in India.
Reason (R): It stripped the Supreme Court of jurisdiction over executive actions and revenue matters.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R is the correct explanation. Stripping the court of jurisdiction over administration and revenue was a statutory restriction on judicial review.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The King-in-Council in London remained the ultimate court of appeal for Indian cases.
Reason (R): The British government wanted to maintain sovereign imperial oversight over both the EIC executive and the judiciary in India.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are true and R is the correct explanation. Bypassing local courts for high-value cases ensured London maintained final imperial control.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Amending Act of 1781:
1. It exempted EIC servants from the Supreme Court's jurisdiction for their official acts.
2. It abolished the Sadar Diwani Adalat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Act recognized the Sadar Diwani Adalat, putting it under the Governor-General-in-Council's authority.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the revenue administration after 1781:
1. Revenue collection acts were completely protected from Supreme Court intervention.
2. The Supreme Court could still adjudicate revenue collections if the EIC Governor-General gave consent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Statement 1 is correct. The exclusion of revenue was absolute under the Act and did not depend on the Governor-General's consent. Statement 2 is therefore incorrect.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding personal laws under the 1781 Act:
1. Hindu law was applied if the plaintiff was Hindu.
2. Mohammedan law was applied if the defendant was Muslim.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Statement 2 is correct. The law applied was determined by the religion of the *defendant*, not the plaintiff. If the defendant was Muslim, Islamic law was applied. Thus, statement 1 is incorrect.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding appellate rules under the 1781 Act:
1. Provincial civil cases under £5,000 lay to the GG-in-Council.
2. Cases of £5,000 and above could be appealed to the King-in-Council.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct, describing the appellate hierarchy and the £5,000 threshold.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the constitutional nature of the 1781 Act:
1. It introduced a system of checks and balances on the executive.
2. It weakened the judiciary's power of judicial review over administration.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Statement 2 is correct. The Act did not introduce checks on the executive; instead, it immunized the executive, which weakened the judiciary's review power. Thus, statement 1 is incorrect.

masteryZone.q: Why were revenue matters excluded from the Supreme Court's jurisdiction by the Act of 1781?
masteryZone.sol: To ensure that EIC's revenue collections were not delayed or paralyzed by judicial lawsuits, preserving the financial flow that funded the British colonial empire.

masteryZone.q: Why was the 'defendant's personal law' chosen as the rule in native civil disputes?
masteryZone.sol: Because applying the defendant's law ensured fairness under English legal tradition (the accused/defendant is judged by their own standard) and prevented native religious unrest.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Act of 1781 allow appeals to the King-in-Council in London for high-value cases?
masteryZone.sol: To maintain imperial sovereignty and ensure that the ultimate legal and commercial decisions of the colony were supervised directly by the British Crown.

masteryZone.q: How did the Act of Settlement 1781 resolve the deadlock over regulation-making?
masteryZone.sol: By exempting regulations made by the Governor-General-in-Council for the provincial courts and councils from the requirement of registration in the Supreme Court.

masteryZone.q: How did the Act protect provincial magistrates from the Supreme Court?
masteryZone.sol: By declaring that no action could be brought in the Supreme Court against provincial judges or officers for acts done in their judicial capacity.

masteryZone.q: How did the Act of 1781 impact the balance of power between Warren Hastings and the judiciary?
masteryZone.sol: It tilted the balance heavily in Warren Hastings' favor by exempting his council's official actions from the Supreme Court's jurisdiction.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: Under the 1781 Act, native residents of Calcutta had to bring civil suits to the Supreme Court, which applied personal laws. What does this case study show about the legal status of Calcutta inhabitants?
masteryZone.sol: It shows that Calcutta inhabitants were treated as direct subjects of the British Crown court, unlike provincial inhabitants who were under EIC provincial courts.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: In 1782, a plaintiff sued an EIC tax collector in the Supreme Court for seizing property. The court dismissed the case citing the 1781 Act. What does this case study show about the limitations on the rule of law?
masteryZone.sol: It shows that the rule of law was limited in colonial India to protect EIC revenues, leaving native taxpayers with no judicial remedy against official collections.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: A Governor-General's regulation in 1783 was implemented in Bihar without Supreme Court approval. What does this case study show about legislative authority?
masteryZone.sol: It shows that the Governor-General-in-Council had independent legislative power over the provinces, free from judicial veto, establishing the system of Regulation Laws.

masteryZone.q: Explain the concept of 'Act of Settlement' in colonial constitutional development.
masteryZone.sol: It is an act designed to 'settle' or resolve a constitutional crisis. In 1781, it settled the division of power by immunizing the EIC executive and revenue collections from the Crown's Supreme Court.

masteryZone.q: Explain the difference in appellate routes before and after the Amending Act of 1781.
masteryZone.sol: Before 1781, the route was vague and the Supreme Court claimed appellate rights. After 1781, provincial appeals went directly to the Governor-General-in-Council (Sadar Diwani Adalat), bypassing the Supreme Court.

masteryZone.q: Explain the significance of 'Executive Immunity' introduced by the 1781 Act.
masteryZone.sol: Executive immunity meant that the Governor-General and his Council could not be sued in India for actions taken as part of their official duties, protecting administration from judicial veto.
